summary: E passes: CLAIMS.md:70 [lead] (anatomy cb22e610 SERIAL at low, g 0.338/0.324, t4/t0 0.49, not ingest-bound) reopens the K-pair shelf CLAIMS.md:69; CLAIMS.md:55's reopen (a different low-class kernel) is met; board/blob unmoved. K-pair is a sound TLP/latency lever for what was measured, but a flat or OFF result is readable only if the gate also runs a stagger arm, prints w13 and w2 separately, and captures ptxas wgmma-serialization warnings.
justification: Low w13 warm pop:1: t0 293.6, t1 194.4, t2 191.1, t3 290.6, t4 145.1, t5 158.6 us; ~512 stages/CTA at 0.573 us. The super-serial reading (t0 > t1+t2-t5) is at least partly a model artifact: modes 1 and 2 are each floored by the producer's pace (ft: t2 0.586 us/stage vs t4 0.587), so t1+t2-t5 undercounts the consumer chain; the data fit a plain serial per-WG chain (dq_stage, 8 dependent k16 wgmmas, wgmma_wait<0>, mbarrier round trip), latency-bound with the producer idle half the time (t4/t0 0.41-0.65): the regime a TLP lever attacks. K-pair halves each WG's dependent MMA chain (8 -> 4 k16) and doubles independent consumer chains per SMSP; its floor is ~t4 or the dequant issue rate, not max(t1,t2). V64 occ2 (LESSONS:180, 0.887 vs 0.984) is a fair analog. Prior differences are real (one shared ring, one item, 128-route slab kept; not CLAIMS:44 item ping-pong, not CLAIMS:68 wait<1> ring). WEAKEST LINK: pairs likely phase-locked (same full[s], producer ahead, named_bar(1,512) per item re-syncs), leaving only chain-halving and latency hiding. SECOND RISK: 112 regs at NB 128; ptxas may silently serialize wgmmas (C7510/C7512) without a spill. COST: reduction 64 KB/item + ~6 named barriers ~0.5 us vs ~37 (w13) / ~18 (w2) us per item, 1.5-3%. Prepare fine (fsilu+w2st end ~176 s). VALUE RE-SIZE: CLAIMS:70's 13.32% applies a 40% all-row share to a class touching only turn_1 rows; recovering all of g at sliding turn_1 (x0.823, share 0.217) and full turn_1 (x0.884, share 0.117) caps low at ~5.2% headline; high (g 0.21, rega 1076.5 of 2246.9 us) caps ~3%. gain ~2.1 (1.6 if high OFF) stands; p 0.2 -> ~0.3, EV ~0.6%, user-requested.

Fold into _rega_kp_phase: (1) a runtime STAGGER argument (uniform branch, no new instantiation) gated as a second arm with stagger 0: pair 1 starts each item one stage late, or the pairs alternate dequant/MMA via an ordered named-barrier pair; (2) capture and print the kp build's ptxas stderr plus a SASS grep for WARPGROUP.DEPBAR count per k loop, with regs and local (CLAIMS:68's reopen evidence); (3) w13 and w2 ratios printed separately with per-GEMM dispatch; (4) add the rega-lo/w2st skew-guard routing (pop:2.2, ~1.83x uniform, <= 1.00 every round) to the gate. If (1) is not folded in and the run is flat, the follow-up is the stagger arm, not a [refuted] line.

open_questions: Is the super-serial excess real contention or the producer floor in modes 1 and 2? Compare t1/t2 per stage to t4 per stage (low 0.380 / 0.373 vs 0.283; ft t2 = t4). If the floor model holds, g underestimates what a TLP lever can recover (floor ~t4) and overestimates a pure overlap lever (floor max(t1,t2)).

Sibling worth minting: ordered anti-phase of master's two existing consumer WGs at stage granularity (FA3-style named barriers): WG0 issues wgmmas while WG1 dequantizes, at 232 regs, no K split, no reduction, bit-exact, full slab and ring kept; attacks the overlap gap toward max(t1,t2) = 194 us.
